text: Intraset rest training (also called cluster sets or rest-pause training) is essentially a catch-all phrase; there are myriad ways to carry out the strategy from a practical standpoint. General recommendations for this strategy prescribe rest intervals of 10 to 30 seconds between repetitions (39), although no guidelines exist for the point at which these rest intervals should be implemented during the course of a set. Moreover, the strategy can be performed in an undulating manner in which resistance is progressively increased in a pyramid-type fashion or as an ascending cluster set in which resistance is increased on each successive repetition (39).
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
